title: Wiki — 山谷飛行（第一幕）
frame_numbering: 1-based. File 0001.webp = Blender frame 1. progress p (0..1) -> frame = 1 + round(p * 299).
deterministic: Camera has one keyframe on every frame (linear). Water, mist, waterfall, koi, boat and birds are keyframed or driven by the frame number only. Any frame renders identically in any order, so forward and reverse scrubbing show the same image.

mobile.codec: H.264 High, yuv420p, MP4 (moov at start / +faststart)
mobile.camera_note: Separate portrait camera that shares FlightCam's animation (same path, same rotation). Only the lens fit differs: 28 mm with VERTICAL sensor fit, so the portrait frame shows the centre of the landscape view plus more sky and water. Not a stretched or cropped landscape video.
mobile.encoder: ffmpeg libx264 -preset slow -crf 21 -g 8 -keyint_min 8 -sc_threshold 0 -bf 0 -an, from lossless PNG frames
mobile.keyframe_positions: every 8th frame exactly (0, 8, 16, ... 296), no scene-cut keyframes

camera_motion.summary: Starts 2.2 m above the lake looking down 40 deg at koi, tilts up to the horizon while accelerating, cruises low along an S-shaped river between karst towers, then slows and tilts up 12 deg toward the waterfall, stopping about 80 m in front of it.
camera_motion.units: metres; Blender world space (Z up, valley runs along +Y)
camera_motion.per_frame_path: camera_path.json (location + rotation for all 300 frames); camera_analysis.json (also pitch, yaw, waterfall and koi visibility per frame)
camera_motion.next_scene_link: Scene 2 (climb along the waterfall) should start from the frame-300 transform above, with the same lens.

events.note: Top-down view of 11 koi through clear water; last koi leaves frame at 23 (measured).
Pitch -23 deg -> +0.75 deg; horizon passes -5 deg at frame 50.
Measured: waterfall top inside the camera frame. It is distant and soft in mist at first.
Constant +2 deg pitch, about 19-25 m/s along the river bends; towers pass on both sides.
Decelerates and tilts up to +12 deg; waterfall fills about 97% of frame height at 300.
Hand-off pose for the next scene.
